title: Drywall Load Size by IICRC Class in Water Damage Mitigation Tear-Out
content:
Within Water Damage Mitigation, the height of a flood cut follows the IICRC class of the intrusion, and that height decides how many linear feet of cut drywall fill one pickup-truck load on the job's tear-out debris haul-off line.

## Standard
The cut height follows the IICRC class of the intrusion: on a Class 3 or Class 4 job carrying flood cut lines, where walls are wet well above the floor, the drywall load size is 80 linear feet per load; on a Class 2 job carrying flood cut lines it is 100 linear feet per load; on any other job no class-based drywall load size applies.

The drywall load size is the number of linear feet of cut drywall (the total linear feet on the job's flood cut lines) counted as one load. The class is the IICRC water class recorded on the job.

## Table
| IICRC class on the job record | Job carries flood cut lines | Drywall load size under this standard |
|---|---|---|
| Class 3 | yes | 80 linear feet per load |
| Class 4 | yes | 80 linear feet per load |
| Class 2 | yes | 100 linear feet per load |
| Class 1 | yes | no class-based size |
| any class | no | no class-based size |

## Illustration (hypothetical)
A Class 3 intrusion from a failed upstairs supply line leaves 200 linear feet of flood cut on the job: at 80 linear feet per load, the cut drywall amounts to 2.5 loads; on a Class 2 job the same run would amount to 2 loads at 100 linear feet per load.
